دوسری جانب جمعہ ہی کے روز وفاقی حکومت کی جانب سے بھی سپریم کورٹ کے فیصلے خلاف دائر کردہ نظرثانی درخواست پر عائد اعتراضات دور کرنے کے بعد دوبارہ عدالت عظمیٰ سے رجوع کیا گیا ہے۔

گذشتہ شب پیش آئے واقعے اور اس کے بعد سامنے آنے والے بیانات کی بنیاد پر سیاسی تجزیہ کاروں کا کہنا ہے کہ عمران خان کو شفا ہسپتال کے بجائے پمز لے جانے کے حکومتی فیصلے نے ناصرف قانونی سوالات کو جنم دیا ہے بلکہ پہلے سے موجود سیاسی کشیدگی میں بھی اضافہ کیا ہے۔
output: Former Prime Minister Imran Khan was taken to PIMS Hospital instead of Shifa Hospital. This went against an order from the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court is Pakistan's highest court. This issue increased political tension between the government and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf is a political party. The party announced it would go to the Supreme Court on August 22. It wanted the court to take action against the government for contempt of court. Contempt of court means the court takes action when someone does not obey a court order. The party said it would keep its September 27 protest. It also hinted it would speed up its protest movement. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf leader Zulfi Bukhari spoke to BBC Urdu. He accused the government of violating the Supreme Court's order. A review petition was filed against the Supreme Court's decision. The federal government cleared the objections to that petition. Then it went to the Supreme Court again. A review petition means asking the same court to look again at a decision. Political analysts say the decision to take Imran Khan to PIMS instead of Shifa Hospital raised legal questions and increased political tension.

instruction: Explain this news in Urdish (Urdu in Roman letters, mixed with common English words) for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
Ahmed al Madhoun looked like a man who, despite the hardship, loved life. A cheeky, chunky little fellow with an exuberant smile.

From her partially destroyed home in Gaza City, his mother Majdiya shows us videos of him on her phone.

In one, Ahmed is cuddling a kitten. He sticks out his tongue and squeals with glee. In another, he belly flops into a swimming pool, before emerging from the water grinning from ear to ear.

"Everyone was his friend," Majdiya tells the BBC. "He was loved wherever he went, and he always had a smile on his face."

But Ahmed, who has Down's syndrome, is missing. The 21-year-old disappeared in May 2025 after popping to the local shop.

At the time, the war in Gaza between Hamas and Israel was raging.

That day there were Israeli strikes in the area, and Majdiya fears her son is dead. But she doesn't know for certain.

"My God, I am not at peace," she says. "I have not lost hope but whether they find him alive or dead, buried under the rubble, only then will I be at peace."

Pain like Majdiya's is felt by mothers all over Gaza.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign, including about 1,200 since a ceasefire was announced last October, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry - figures considered reliable by the UN.

Israeli media reported in January that a senior Israeli security source saidthe military accepts the figures are accurate.

But the true number of dead Palestinians could be significantly higher. The health ministry's death toll doesn't count bodies buried under the rubble, meaning many of the missing are not part of the count.

The Red Cross says it has received more than 5,000 requests to trace missing people who could be buried amid the destruction. The Civil Defence agency in Gaza believes the number of missing people is over 8,000.

Bodies are being discovered on a daily basis.

Earlier this month, a mass funeral took place in Gaza City for more than a hundred people killed in an Israeli attack in 2023. Their remains were only recently recovered and identified, allowing them to be laid to rest.

The Red Cross says recovering bodies is difficult given the scale of the destruction and a lack of bulldozers.

In many cases, identifying the remains is also challenging when people have been dead for so long and with a lack of DNA testing, due to Israeli restrictions on what can enter Gaza.

Ahmed al Madhoun's family knows he may well have been killed - but they also fear he may have been detained by Israeli security forces.

Over almost three years of war, Israeli forces have detained approximately 7,000 Palestinians from Gaza, more than 5,000 of whom were later released without ever being charged,according to the Israel-based Public Committee Against Torture,external.

As of this month, around 1,300 detainees from Gaza were being held in Israeli jails without charge or trial, according to the Israeli human rights group HaMoked. The group says these figures do not include Gaza detainees held directly by the Israeli military.

Palestinian families have frequently not been notified by Israel of the arrest or whereabouts of their relatives, according to HaMoked and other rights groups - forcing many to rely on NGOs and lawyers to help track them down.

The BBC has asked the IDF and Israel Prison Service (IPS) about their reported failure to contact relatives of those they have detained.

Israeli authorities have previously said prolonged detentions were due to wartime security grounds and rejected claims that detentions are arbitrary.

Aida al Drimli from the Sabra district of Gaza City, shows us a picture of her son, Mahmoud, a fresh-faced young man draped in a Palestinian scarf.

"He was a calm well-mannered young man," Aida says. "He loved everyone and everyone loved him."

Mahmoud disappeared in 2024. His family feared he had been killed in an Israeli attack.

"His father would go to the hospitals and look at the bodies," Aida tells us. "But I couldn't face it. I was completely devastated."

But then this summer a photo emerged on social media showing two Israeli soldiers posing with a Palestinian detainee, blindfolded and bound.
output: Ahmed al Madhoun 21 saal ka young man tha. Usay Down's syndrome tha. May 2025 mein woh Gaza City mein missing ho gaya. Us ki maa Majdiya ne BBC ko bataya ke Ahmed ko har jagah log pasand karte the. Woh hamesha smile karta tha. Hamas Gaza par hukumat karta hai. Yeh ek Palestinian group hai. Us ki health ministry ke mutabiq Israel ki military campaign ke baad Gaza mein 73,000 se zyada log maaray gaye. In mein woh taqreeban 1,200 log bhi shamil hain jo pichhle October mein ceasefire ke elaan ke baad maaray gaye. Ceasefire, yaani truce, ka matlab hai larai rok dena. Red Cross ek international aid organization hai. Usay 5,000 se zyada missing logon ko dhoondhne ki requests mili hain. Gaza's Civil Defence, yaani local emergency aid team, kehta hai ke missing logon ki tadaad 8,000 se zyada hai. Red Cross ne kaha ke malbe se jism nikalna mushkil hai. Us ne yeh bhi kaha ke Israeli restrictions ki wajah se DNA testing ki kami hai. Israeli forces ne taqreeban 7,000 Palestinians ko Gaza se pakra. In mein se 5,000 se zyada bina ilzaam chhor diye gaye. Bina ilzaam ya muqadma ka matlab hai ke kisi ne nahi bataya ke kis crime mein pakra gaya. Aur na court mein case suna gaya. HaMoked ek human rights group hai. Us ke mutabiq is mahine Gaza ke taqreeban 1,300 qaidis Israeli jails mein bina ilzaam ya muqadma rakhe gaye the. Aida al Drimli ne bataya ke un ka beta Mahmoud 2024 mein missing hua. Is summer, social media par ek photo aayi jis mein do Israeli soldiers ek Palestinian qaidi ke saath thay.

instruction: Explain this news in English for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
پیر کے روز جیسے جیسے انڈین ریاست مغربی بنگال اسمبلی انتخابات کے نتائج کے رجحانات آنے لگے، دارالحکومت کولکتہ اور ریاست کے دوسرے علاقوں میں جے شری رام کے نعرے گونجنے لگے۔

بنگال کی تاریخ میں ایسا شاید ہی پہلے دیکھا گیا تھا۔ عام طور پر بنگال کی سڑکوں اور گیلوں میں لال سلام، جے بانگلا، مائے ماٹی مانُس، جے دُرگا اور جے ماں کالی جیسے سیاسی اور مذہبی نعرے سننے کو ملتے رہے ہیں۔

لیکن اب بنگال کا سیاسی اور سماجی منظر نامہ بدل چکا ہے۔ مغربی بنگال میں اقتدار حاصل کرنا تو دور کی بات، اس کے قریب پہنچنا بھی بھارتیہ جنتا پارٹی (بی جے پی) جیسی قوم پرست سیاسی جماعتوں کے لیے ایک ناممکن سا خواب معلوم ہوتا تھا۔

لیکن یہی بی جے پی حالیہ انتخابی نتائج کے بعد ریاست کی سب سے بڑی سیاسی پارٹی بن کر ابھری ہے۔ اس رپورٹ کے لکھے جانے تک، الیکشن کمیشن آف انڈیا کے مطابق، 294 میں سے بی جے پی نے 206 نشستیں حاصل کر لی ہیں، جو کہ ہر اعتبار سے تاریخی اہمیت کا حامل ہے۔

واضح رہے کہ ریاست میں حکومت سازی کے لیے کُل نشستوں کی نصف تعداد (یعنی 147) سے ایک نشست زیادہ کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے۔ یوں، 206 نشستوں پر کامیابی حاصل کرنے والی بی جے پی آسانی سے حکومت بنا سکتی ہے۔

گذشتہ اسمبلی انتخابات میں بی جے پی کو صرف 77 جبکہ ممتا بینرجی کی قیادت والی پارٹی ترنمول کانگریس (ٹی ایم سی) کو 213 نشستوں پر کامیابی ملی تھی۔ تاہم اس بار ٹی ایم سی صرف 81 نشستوں پر کامیاب ہوئی ہے۔

غور طلب بات یہ ہے کہ خود ممتا بینرجی کو اپنی نشست پر بھی شکست کا سامنا کرنا پڑا ہے۔ وہ اپنے روایتی اسمبلی حلقہ بھوانی پور سے بی جے پی رہنما سویندو ادھیکاری سے 15 ہزار ووٹوں سے ہار گئی ہیں۔

اس سوال کے جواب میں سینیئر صحافی اور سیاسی تجزیہ کار نیلانجن مُکھوپادھیائے نے بی بی سی کو بتایا کہ بنیادی طور پر اس کی دو وجوہات ہیں۔ 'اول، ممتا حکومت کے خلاف اینٹی انکمبنسی (یعنی ووٹر کی ناراضی) اور دوم، سپیشل انٹینسیو ریویژن (ایس آئی آر) کے عمل کے دوران بڑی تعداد میں ووٹرز کا نام لسٹ سے نکالا جانا۔' ان کے مطابق ممتا بینرجی کی گذشتہ 15 سالہ حکومت کے دوران بڑھتی ہوئی بدعنوانی اور تشدد کے واقعات نے انھیں ریاست میں غیر مقبول بنا دیا تھا، جس کا فائدہ بی جے پی نے اس انتخاب میں اٹھایا۔
output: On Monday, when trends in the assembly election results started coming in in India’s state of West Bengal, slogans of Jai Shri Ram began echoing in Kolkata and other areas of the state. In Bengal, slogans like Lal Salam, Jai Bangla, Maa Mati Manush, Jai Durga and Jai Maa Kali have usually been heard. According to the Election Commission of India, which holds elections in India, out of 294 seats, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won 206 seats. To form a government in the state, one more seat than 147 is needed, so the BJP can form a government with 206 seats. In the last assembly elections, the BJP got 77 seats and the Trinamool Congress (TMC), led by Mamata Banerjee, got 213 seats. This time the TMC won only 81 seats. Mamata Banerjee lost her traditional assembly constituency, Bhabanipur, to BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari by 15,000 votes. An assembly constituency is an area where voters choose one member of the state assembly. Nilanjan Mukhopadhyay told the BBC that one reason against the Mamata government is anti-incumbency. Anti-incumbency means people want a change from the current government. The second reason is that voters’ names were removed from the list during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). SIR is a special process of checking voter lists, in which some names can be removed from the list.

instruction: Explain this news in English for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
'سیاست ممکنات کا کھیل ہے' اور 'سیاست میں کچھ دائمی نہیں ہوتا۔' یہ مثل پاکستان کی سیاسی تاریخ پر پوری اترتی ہیں۔ پاکستان کی 76 سالہ تاریخ میں کئی ادوار آئے اور گزر گئے مگر ان تمام میں کچھ چیزیں مشترک دکھائی دیتی ہیں۔

چاہے وہ کسی فوجی ڈکٹیٹر کا دور ہو یا منتخب حکومت کا۔۔۔ ملکی سیاست میں نظریہ ضرورت اور اسٹیبلشمنٹ کا اثر و رسوخ غالب نظر آتا ہے۔

کبھی عدلیہ نے کسی منتخب حکومت کو چلتا کیا تو کبھی کوئی فوجی سربراہ وزیر اعظم ہاؤس کی دیواریں پھلانگتا ہوا اندر چلا آیا۔ اسی دوران گذشتہ ایک دہائی کے دوران ملکی سیاست میں ایک نئی اصطلاح 'لاڈلے' نے جنم لیا۔

یہ اصطلاح اُس جماعت یا سیاسی لیڈر کے لیے استعمال کی جاتی جسے، سیاسی جماعتوں کی رائے میں، ملکی اسٹیبلشمنٹ کا آشیر باد حاصل ہوتا۔ مگر سیاسی پنڈتوں کا کہنا ہے کہ سنہ 1950 سے ہی پاکستانی سیاست میں کوئی نہ کوئی 'لاڈلہ' رہا ہے۔

اگرچہ دنیا کے دیگر ممالک میں سیاسی رہنما اپنی طرز حکمرانی سے عوام کے 'لاڈلے' ہوتے ہیں لیکن سیاسی تجزیہ کاروں کے مطابق پاکستان میں یہ اختیار اسٹیبلشمنٹ کے پاس ہے۔

اگر حالیہ سیاسی تاریخ کی بات کی جائے تو سنہ 2013 میں پاکستان تحریک انصاف کے چیئرمین عمران خان کے لیے سیاسی جماعتوں نے 'لاڈلہ' کی اصطلاح استعمال کی مگر آج مسلم لیگ ن کے قائد نواز شریف کو مقدمات میں ملنے والے عدالتی 'ریلیف' کے بعد یہی خطاب ان کے لیے استعمال کیا جا رہا ہے۔

پنجاب کی نگراں حکومت کی جانب سے نواز شریف کے خلاف العزیزیہ ریفرنس میں ان کی سزا معطل کیے جانے کے بعد سیاسی حلقوں میں اس بحث نے زور پکڑ کیا ہے کہ کیا 'اب لاڈلہ بدل' گیا ہے۔

چند برس قبل نواز شریف اور ان کی جماعت مسلم لیگ ن 'زیر عتاب' تھی۔ پانامہ کیس میں سپریم کورٹ کے لارجر بینچ کے حکم پر ستمبر 2017 میں مسلم لیگ ن کے قائد میاں نواز شریف کے خلاف اسلام آباد کی احتساب عدالت میں تین ریفرنسز دائر کیے گئے اور نواز شریف اپنی بیٹی مریم نواز اور داماد کیپٹن ریٹائرڈ صفدر کے ساتھ پیشی کے لیے آتے تھے۔

میاں نواز شریف، مریم نواز اور کیپٹن صفدر عدالت کا وقت شروع ہونے سے 15، 20 منٹ قبل ہی کمرۂ عدالت میں پہنچ جاتے اور جج کی آمد کا انتظار کرتے کیونکہ ان کے وکلا کے بقول خدشہ یہ ہوتا تھا کہ اگر وہ دیر سے عدالت پہنچے تو اسی بنیاد پر ان کے ناقابل ضمانت وارنٹ گرفتاری نہ جاری کر دیے جائیں۔

نواز شریف اس وقت تک عدالت میں بیٹھے رہتے جب تک اس دن کی سماعت مکمل نہیں ہو جاتی تھی۔ عدالتی سماعت کے بعد نواز شریف میڈیا سے گفتگو کرتے اور اسٹیبلشمنٹ اور اعلیٰ عدلیہ پر کُھل کر تنقید کرکے اپنے دل کی بھڑاس نکالتے۔

ان ریفرنسز کی سماعت کے دوران قومی احتساب بیورو (نیب) کے پراسیکوٹرز نواز شریف کی مبینہ کرپشن سے متعلق دلائل دیتے اور یہ ثابت کرنے کی کوشش کرتے کہ سابق وزیر اعظم سے بڑا 'بدعنوان سیاست دان' پاکستان کی تاریخ میں نہیں ملتا اور انھی دلائل کی بنیاد پر میاں نواز شریف کو تین میں سے دو ریفرنسز میں سزائیں سنائی گئیں۔

مگر تقریباً چھ برس بعد وطن واپسی پر جب نواز شریف احتساب عدالت کے اُسی جج محمد بشیر کی عدالت میں بطور ملزم پیش ہوئے جنھوں نے سنہ 2018 میں انھیں ایون فیلڈ ریفرنس میں 10 سال قید کی سزا سنائی تھی تو اس مرتبہ وہ وقت سے قبل عدالت آ کر جج کا انتظار نہیں کر رہے تھے بلکہ جج اُن کی آمد کے منتظر تھے۔ اور جیسے ہی وہ پارٹی رہنماؤں کے ساتھ کمرۂ عدالت پہنچے تو انھیں فی الفور حاضری لگوا کر جانے کی اجازت دے دی گئی اور باقی کارروائی ان کی عدم موجودگی میں پوری ہوئی۔

اس کے بعد جب میاں نواز شریف اسلام آباد ہائیکورٹ پہنچے تو وہاں پر بھی ان کے استقبال کے لیے پولیس کے اعلیٰ افسران موجود تھے جنھوں نے نواز شریف، جو اب بھی ایک عدالتی مجرم ہیں، کو ناصرف سیلوٹ کیا بلکہ ہائیکورٹ کی انتظامیہ کی طرف سے انھیں کمرۂ عدالت میں لے کر جانے کے لیے ایک لفٹ مختص کر دی گئی۔
output: For 76 years of Pakistan's history, the establishment has had the strongest influence on politics. By "establishment," we mean the powerful institutions of the state that influence politics. In 2013, political parties used the term "Ladla" (favourite) for Imran Khan, the chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. The caretaker government in Punjab—the temporary government formed before elections—suspended Nawaz Sharif's sentence in the Al-Azizia reference. A reference is a case that is formally filed against someone in court. In September 2017, in the Panama case, the Supreme Court's larger bench—a bigger panel of judges—ordered that three references be filed against Nawaz Sharif in the Accountability Court in Islamabad. Nawaz Sharif used to appear in court with his daughter Maryam Nawaz and his son-in-law Captain (retired) Safdar. In 2018, Judge Muhammad Bashir sentenced Nawaz Sharif to 10 years in prison in the Avenfield reference. About six years later, when Nawaz Sharif returned to the country and appeared in the court of the same judge, Muhammad Bashir, the judge was waiting for him to arrive. At the Islamabad High Court, senior police officers saluted Nawaz Sharif, and a lift was reserved for him.

instruction: Explain this news in English for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
Pakistan's electricity is expensive not because the grid is poorly run, though it often is, but because the country built a power system for an economy that never arrived, financed it on contracts that force everyone to pay whether or not they use the power, and has spent thirty years pushing the cost forward instead of confronting it.

Pull out your last bill and look at the total. If your household uses around 400 units a month, you are paying close to Rs16,000. Less than half of that is for the electricity you use. The rest pays for idle power plants, debt built up because someone upstream did not pay their share, and charges added over the years to plug holes the system kept opening.

Start with the number that explains everything else. Pakistan has 46,600 megawatts of installed capacity, and according to the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority's own data, it used only about a third of that in FY24. Two out of every three megawatts the country built simply sat there. Peak demand rarely goes past 35,000 MW, so every month we pay for power nobody needs. Capacity grew 64 per cent between 2013 and 2024 because planners and investors bet on a manufacturing boom and a fast-growing middle class that never fully showed up.

The reason this keeps getting worse instead of fading away is buried in the contracts themselves. Power producers are paid two ways: a fixed amount just for existing, and a separate amount for whatever they generate. That made sense in the 1990s, when the state had no money to build plants and investors needed a guarantee before risking their own. What nobody accounted for was a rupee that would lose more than 60pc of its value while these obligations stayed tied to the dollar. In FY24 alone, consumers paid Rs46 billion to two plants that produced no power at all. At Rousch Power, the fixed payment alone came to over seven hundred rupees a unit, roughly eighteen times what electricity itself was worth.
output: Electricity in Pakistan is expensive because the country built a power system for an economy that never came. It also paid money under contracts that make everyone pay, whether they use electricity or not. A household that uses 400 units a month pays about Rs16,000. Less than half of that amount is for the electricity it uses. The rest goes to idle power plants, debt, and extra charges. Pakistan's installed capacity is 46,600 MW. Installed capacity means how much electricity the country's power plants can make in total. According to data from the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority, which monitors electricity matters, only about one third of that was used in FY24. Pakistan's peak demand rarely goes above 35,000 MW. Peak demand means the most electricity needed at one time. So every month, payment is made for electricity that nobody needs. Between 2013 and 2024, capacity grew by 64 percent. This happened because planners and investors bet on a boom in manufacturing and a fast-growing middle class that did not fully show up. Power producers are paid in two ways. One is a fixed payment just for existing, and a separate payment is for generating electricity. A fixed payment is money a plant gets just for existing, whether it makes electricity or not. For example, it is like paying a taxi just to keep the car ready, whether you travel or not. The value of the rupee fell by more than 60 percent while these obligations stayed tied to the dollar. In FY24, consumers paid Rs46 billion to two plants that produced no electricity at all. At Rousch Power, the fixed payment alone came to more than 700 rupees per unit, which was about 18 times the actual price of electricity.

In total, governor's rule can remain in place for a maximum of six months.

Meanwhile, under Article 232, which pertains to the proclamation of an emergency, the provincial assembly continues to function as usual. However, if a provincial law conflicts with a federal law enacted by parliament, the latter takes precedence.

Talking to Dawn, lawyer Basil Nabi Malik explained that the chief minister would remain in office during a state of emergency. However, the federal government could assume certain functions of the provincial government.

An emergency also allows the federal government to make provisions it considers necessary and suspend certain constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies. However, as with governor's rule, the federal government cannot assume the powers of a high court.

It also empowers parliament to confer powers and impose duties on federal government officers in the province.

It further stipulates that laws passed by parliament solely on account of the emergency will cease to have effect six months after the emergency ends.

The proclamation of emergency lapses after two months unless it is approved by a resolution of a joint sitting of parliament.

Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency Ahmed Bilal Mehmoob told Dawn that invoking both articles of the Constitution together was an unprecedented move by the federal government.

In his view, this double-barrelled approach was deliberate, since Article 232 alone did not render the provincial assembly dysfunctional.

"In that case, the provincial assembly continues to function but cannot enact any law which contradicts federal legislation. If the provincial assembly continues to work, it can create a nuisance for the governor and his new provincial set-up," he added.

However, Article 234 can be enforced for an indefinite period, and also serves to neuter the provincial assembly. "This was the reason the Centre used both articles in proclamation of emergency in KP," he added.

The Pildat chief, however, noted that under Article 234, the provincial assembly will automatically become functional after six months.
output: Governor's rule — when the federal government runs the province — can last a maximum of 6 months in total. Under Article 232, during a state of emergency, the provincial assembly keeps working as usual. A state of emergency means that in unusual conditions, the government gets some special powers. For example, if a big disaster hits an area, a state of emergency is imposed so the government can make quick decisions. If a provincial law clashes with a federal law made by parliament, the federal law will come first. Lawyer Basil Nabi Malik told Dawn that during a state of emergency, the chief minister will stay in his post. During a state of emergency, the federal government can take over some work of the provincial government, but it cannot take the powers of the high court. Because of the state of emergency, laws made by parliament stop having effect 6 months after the state of emergency ends. The announcement of a state of emergency ends after 2 months, unless it is approved by a resolution of a joint sitting of parliament, meaning both houses sitting together. The head of Pildat, a Pakistani research institute, said that using both articles together in KP was an unusual step. Article 234 is a legal clause that relates to a state of emergency like governor's rule in a province. According to him, under Article 234, the provincial assembly will automatically become active again after 6 months.

پاکستان کے صدر آصف علی زرداری نے پارلیمان کے دونوں ایوانوں سے منظوری کے بعد الیکٹرانک کرائمز کی روک تھام کے لیے پیکا ترمیمی بل 2025 کی توثیق کردی ہے۔

صدر پاکستان نے ڈیجیٹل نیشن پاکستان بل 2025 کی بھی منظوری دے دی ہے۔

صدر مملکت کی جانب سے نے الیکٹرانک کرائمز کی روک تھام (پیکا ترمیمی) بل 2025 پر دستخط کرنے کے بعد یہ بل نافذ العمل ہو گیا ہے۔

یاد رہے کہ وفاقی حکومت نے 22 جنوری کو پیکا ایکٹ ترمیمی بل 2025 قومی اسمبلی میں پیش کیا تھا۔

اس بل کے مطابق جو شخص آن لائن 'فیک نیوز' پھیلانے میں ملوث پایا گیا اسے تین سال قید یا 20 لاکھ تک جرمانے یا دونوں سزائیں دی جا سکیں گی۔

دی پریونشن آف الیکٹرانک کرائم ایکٹ (ترمیمی) بل 2025 میں سیکشن 26 (اے) کا اضافہ کیا گیا ہے، جس کے تحت آن لائن 'جعلی خبروں' کے مرتکب افراد کو سزا دی جائے گی، ترمیمی بل میں کہا گیا ہے کہ جو بھی شخص جان بوجھ کر جھوٹی معلومات پھیلاتا ہے، یا کسی دوسرے شخص کو بھیجتا ہے، جس سے معاشرے میں خوف یا بےامنی پھیل سکتی ہے، تو اسے تین سال تک قید، 20 لاکھ روپے تک جرمانہ یا دونوں سزائیں ہو سکتی ہیں۔

پیکا ایکٹ ترمیمی بل 2025 کے مطابق سوشل میڈیا پروٹیکشن اینڈ ریگولیٹری اتھارٹی کا مرکزی دفتر اسلام آباد میں ہوگا، جبکہ صوبائی دارالحکومتوں میں بھی دفاتر قائم کیے جائیں گے۔

منگل کو جب سینیٹ میں یہ بل پیش کیا گیا تو پی ٹی آئی سمیت حزب مخالف کی جماعتوں نے اجلاس کا بائیکاٹ کیا ہے۔

اس موقع پر قائد حزب اختلاف شبلی فراز کا کہنا تھا کہ یہ بل ایک سیاسی جماعت کے لیے بنایا گیا ہے اس پر بحث اور مشاورت نہیں ہوئی جبکہ قانون بنانے کے لیے کئی ماہ لگ جاتے ہیں۔

ادھر حکمراں جماعت نے جمیعت علمائے اسلام ف کے سینیٹر کامران مرتضیٰ نے اس ترمیم کو مسترد کرتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ 'حکومت پیکا ایکٹ کی شق 29 میں ترمیم کرے کیونکہ اس شق میں کہا گیا ہے کہ اس قانون کے تحت ہونے والے اقدامات کو کسی عدالت یا ایجنسی کے سامنے چیلنج نہیں کیا جا سکتا ہے۔'

instruction: Explain this news in Urdish (Urdu in Roman letters, mixed with common English words) for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کو روس کے ساتھ ڈیزل معاہدے پر بڑھتی ہوئی سیاسی مخالفت کا سامنا ہے، جبکہ ان کی انتظامیہ کو آئندہ چند روز میں یہ فیصلہ بھی کرنا ہے کہ آیا یوکرین جنگ کے باعث روس پر نئی توانائی پابندیاں نافذ کی جائیں یا نہیں۔

صدر ٹرمپ نے گذشتہ ہفتے اعلان کیا تھا کہ روس امریکی اور عالمی منڈیوں کے لیے تین لاکھ میٹرک ٹن سے زیادہ ڈیزل فراہم کرے گا اور اس مقصد کے لیے روسی ڈیزل برآمدات پر عائد بعض پابندیاں نرم کی جائیں گی۔

تاہم اس فیصلے پر ریپبلکن اور ڈیموکریٹس دونوں جماعتوں کے قانون سازوں نے اعتراض اٹھایا ہے۔ 12 امریکی سینیٹرز، جن میں چھ ان کی اپنی جماعت سے تعلق رکھنے والے ریپبلکن بھی شامل ہیں، نے صدر ٹرمپ کو خط لکھ کر مطالبہ کیا ہے کہ روس کے ساتھ یہ معاہدہ فوری طور پر واپس لیا جائے۔ ان کا مؤقف ہے کہ اس اقدام سے روس کو عالمی منڈی میں ڈیزل فروخت کر کے اضافی آمدن حاصل ہوگی، جو بالآخر یوکرین کے خلاف جنگی کارروائیوں کے لیے استعمال ہو سکتی ہے۔

سینیٹرز نے کہا ہے کہ یہ معاہدہ 'امریکہ کے سکیورٹی مفادات کو نقصان پہنچاتا ہے' اور یوکرین کے لیے امریکی حمایت کے مؤقف سے متصادم ہے۔ ان کے مطابق یہ اقدام 'امریکہ کے مخالف کے لیے ایک تحفہ اور اتحادیوں سے بے وفائی' کے مترادف ہے۔

یہ تنازع ایسے وقت میں سامنے آیا ہے جب صدر ٹرمپ کو 18 اکتوبر تک یہ فیصلہ کرنا ہے کہ آیا روسی توانائی کے شعبے پر نئی پابندیاں اور محصولات نافذ کیے جائیں یا قومی مفاد کا حوالہ دیتے ہوئے ان سے استثنیٰ دیا جائے۔

ابتدائی طور پر تین لاکھ ٹن ڈیزل کی فراہمی کے علاوہ، ٹرمپ نے کہا کہ روس نومبر میں پانچ لاکھ ٹن اور اس کے بعد مزید 10 لاکھ ٹن ڈیزل فراہم کرے گا۔

اس کے بعد مزید 30 لاکھ ٹن ڈیزل فراہم کیا جائے گا، جو 'مختصر مدت' میں پہنچایا جائے گا۔ تاہم یہ روسی ریفائنریوں کی حالت پر منحصر ہو گا جنھیں دونوں ممالک کے درمیان جاری جنگ کے دوران یوکرین نے نشانہ بنایا ہے۔

ٹرمپ نے اپنے سوشل میڈیا پلیٹ فارم ٹروتھ سوشل پر ایک پوسٹ میں لکھا: 'امریکیوں، خاص طور پر ہمارے عظیم کسانوں، مویشی پالنے والوں اور ٹرک ڈرائیوروں کے لیے کم قیمتیں میری سب سے بڑی ترجیح ہیں۔'

روس کے نائب وزیر اعظم الیگزینڈر نوواک نے سرکاری خبر رساں ادارے تاس سے گفتگو میں ان اعداد و شمار کی تصدیق کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ مستقبل میں برآمدات کا حجم ماہانہ 30 لاکھ ٹن تک پہنچ سکتا ہے۔

یوکرین کے صدر ولادیمیر زیلنسکی نے اس معاہدے کو پوتن کے لیے ایک تحفہ قرار دیتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ یہ 'ایسی جنگ میں سرمایہ کاری کے مترادف ہے جسے ختم ہونا چاہیے۔'

اطلاعات کے مطابق اس معاہدے کے تحت امریکی محکمہ خزانہ سات اپریل تک روسی ڈیزل کی برآمدات پر عائد پابندیاں معطل کر رہا ہے، تاہم امریکی بینکوں میں موجود اثاثوں سمیت دیگر اثاثے بدستور منجمد رہیں گے۔

منگل کو صحافیوں سے گفتگو میں صدر ٹرمپ سے پوچھا گیا کہ کیا کسی نے انھیں بتایا ہے کہ اس معاہدے سے حاصل ہونے والی آمدن روس مزید ہتھیار یا بم خریدنے کے لیے استعمال کر سکتا ہے؟ اس پر ٹرمپ نے جواب دیا، 'نہیں، کسی نے مجھے ایسا کچھ نہیں بتایا۔'

ان کا کہنا تھا کہ یہ معاہدہ صرف امریکہ ہی نہیں بلکہ عالمی منڈی کے لیے بھی فائدہ مند ثابت ہوگا۔

مگر ہر کوئی اس معاہدے کا مخالف نہیں۔ ریپبلکن تھامس میسی، جنھوں نے ٹرمپ کے ساتھ کئی معاملات پر اختلاف کیا ہے، نے کہا کہ امریکہ کو 'تمام پیٹرولیئم مصنوعات پر سے پابندیاں ہٹانی چاہیے۔'

ٹرمپ کے وزیر خزانہ سکاٹ بیسنٹ نے فاکس نیوز کو بتایا کہ یہ معاہدہ موجودہ قانونی چینلز کے ذریعے کام کرے گا جس کا مقصد قیمتوں کو کم کرنا ہے اور یہ کہ اگر کانگریس میں کوئی اس سے اتفاق نہیں کرتا تو یہ غلط ہے۔

فروری کے اواخر میں ایران کے خلاف امریکی و اسرائیلی جنگ شروع ہونے کے بعد سے عالمی سطح پر ایندھن کی قیمتوں میں اضافہ ہوا ہے۔ اس لڑائی نے خام تیل کی سپلائی میں شدید خلل ڈالا ہے جس سے پیٹرول اور ڈیزل کی قیمتیں دنیا بھر میں بڑھی ہیں۔

President Trump ne kaha tha ke Russia American aur world markets ko 300,000 metric tons se zyada diesel dega. 12 US senators ne demand kiya ke deal foran wapas li jaye. In mein 6 Republicans bhi shamil hain. Senators US parliament ke ek hisse ke members hote hain. Republican America ki ek bari political party hai. President Trump ko 18 October tak decide karna hai ke Russia ke energy sector par nayi sanctions lagayein ya nahi. Sanctions kisi mulk par trade aur paise ke mamlat mein lagne wali sazayen hoti hain. President Trump ko yeh bhi decide karna hai ke tariffs lagane hain ya nahi. Tariffs woh extra taxes hote hain jo bahar se aane wali cheezon par lagte hain. For example, agar bahar se aane wali car par tariff lage to woh mehngi ho jati hai. Ya phir woh mulk ke faide ka hawala de kar exemption dein. Exemption ka matlab hai ke is mamle mein chhoot mil jaye. Trump ne kaha ke Russia November mein 500,000 tons aur uske baad mazeed 1 million tons diesel dega. Russia ke Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak ne TASS ko bataya ke aage chal kar bahar bheji jane wali diesel monthly 3 million tons tak pahunch sakti hai. TASS Russia ki news agency hai. Ukraine ke President Volodymyr Zelensky ne deal ko Putin ke liye gift kaha. American Automobile Association (AAA) ke mutabiq America mein diesel ki average price 6.28 dollars (4.74 pounds) per gallon hai.

ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Den­tal Council has rescheduled the National Regist­ration Examination (NRE) Step-I from Oct 11 to Nov 8 due to unavoidable circumstances and now foreign medical graduates will face a nearly monthlong delay.

In a notification dated Oct 5, the PMDC cited "unavoidable circumstan­ces" for the move and said Step-1 of the NRE exam will now be held on Nov 8.

A senior PMDC official told Dawn on Wednesday that the decision was made due to the prevailing political situation and possible road closures.

The rescheduling comes after the PTI on Oct 4 launched a long march from Khyber Pakhtu­nkhwa towards Islama­bad, despite warnings from the federal government against such a move.

NRE is a mandatory requirement under an Act of Parliament, aimed at ensuring transparency, standardisation, and quality in medical and dental education and professional practice in Pakistan.

The National University of Medical Sciences in Rawalpindi is entrusted with conducting NRE to "ensure credibility, integrity, and transparency," according to the PMDC.

The exam is conducted in two steps at least twice a year in accordance with the approved NRE standards, structure, and syllabus, and as per a curriculum at par with the medicine and dentistry degrees in Pakistan.

Foreign medical graduates who have earned degrees in medicine or dentistry in languages other than English have to clear two steps or the NRE exam in order to start a house job and get a licence to practise in Pakistan.

In total, governor's rule can remain in place for a maximum of six months.

Meanwhile, under Article 232, which pertains to the proclamation of an emergency, the provincial assembly continues to function as usual. However, if a provincial law conflicts with a federal law enacted by parliament, the latter takes precedence.

Talking to Dawn, lawyer Basil Nabi Malik explained that the chief minister would remain in office during a state of emergency. However, the federal government could assume certain functions of the provincial government.

An emergency also allows the federal government to make provisions it considers necessary and suspend certain constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies. However, as with governor's rule, the federal government cannot assume the powers of a high court.

It also empowers parliament to confer powers and impose duties on federal government officers in the province.

It further stipulates that laws passed by parliament solely on account of the emergency will cease to have effect six months after the emergency ends.

The proclamation of emergency lapses after two months unless it is approved by a resolution of a joint sitting of parliament.

Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency Ahmed Bilal Mehmoob told Dawn that invoking both articles of the Constitution together was an unprecedented move by the federal government.

In his view, this double-barrelled approach was deliberate, since Article 232 alone did not render the provincial assembly dysfunctional.

"In that case, the provincial assembly continues to function but cannot enact any law which contradicts federal legislation. If the provincial assembly continues to work, it can create a nuisance for the governor and his new provincial set-up," he added.

However, Article 234 can be enforced for an indefinite period, and also serves to neuter the provincial assembly. "This was the reason the Centre used both articles in proclamation of emergency in KP," he added.

The Pildat chief, however, noted that under Article 234, the provincial assembly will automatically become functional after six months.
output: Governor's rule, yani jab federal government province ko chalati hai, total milakar zyada se zyada 6 months tak reh sakta hai. Article 232 ke under, emergency mein provincial assembly pehle ki tarah kaam karti rehti hai. Emergency ka matlab hai ke jab halat normal na hon, government ko kuch khaas powers mil jati hain. Misal ke tor par, agar kisi area mein bari aafat aa jaye to emergency lagai jati hai, taake government foran faislay kar sake. Agar provincial law parliament ke banaye federal law se takraye, to federal law pehle chalega. Lawyer Basil Nabi Malik ne Dawn ko bataya ke emergency mein chief minister apne post par rahega. Emergency mein federal government provincial government ke kuch kaam apne haath mein le sakti hai, lekin high court ke powers nahi le sakti. Emergency ki wajah se parliament ke banaye laws, emergency khatam hone ke 6 months baad kaam karna band kar dete hain. Emergency ka elaan 2 months baad khatam ho jata hai, magar ye ke parliament ke joint sitting, yani dono houses ke ek saath baithne, ki resolution se approve ho jaye. Pildat, ek Pakistani research institute, ke head ne kaha ke KP mein dono articles ka ek saath use ek unusual step tha. Article 234 ek legal clause hai jo province mein Governor's rule jaisi emergency se related hai. Un ke mutabiq, Article 234 ke under provincial assembly 6 months baad khud ba khud phir se active ho jayegi.

PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Wednesday rejected a petition filed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi challenging proceedings initiated against him by the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) for allegedly violating the election code of conduct during by-elections in Haripur in November 2025.

A bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali pronounced a short order dismissing the petition without touching the question of the ECP's jurisdiction in light of an earlier court order.

The detailed judgement will be issued later.

With the dismissal of the petition, a stay order earlier granted in favour of Mr Afridi also stands vacated.

Following the preliminary hearing of the petition earlier this year, the court had ordered, "In the meanwhile, the respondent-ECP may proceed with the matter; however, it shall not pass any final order adverse to the petitioner (Sohail Afridi) till further orders."

The development assumes significance amid growing tensions between KP and federal governments over the ongoing protest march.

A panel of lawyers appeared for the petitioner, including Adnan Ali, Bashir Khan Wazir, Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah and Inam Yousafzai. The ECP was represented by Additional Director General (Law) Khurram Shehzad and Additional Director (Law) Samran Jehangir, while Barrister Sajeel Sheharyar Swati appeared for the complainant against Mr Afridi before the ECP.

In November last year, the chief minister and by-election candidate Shehrnaz Omar Ayub, backed by PTI, had challenged notices issued to them by the ECP for allegedly violating the election code of conduct.

Mr Afridi had challenged a notice issued to him by the ECP on Nov 20, accusing him of delivering a provocative speech against government functionaries in connection with the by-election in NA-18 Haripur.

The ECP contended that the CM's speech was contrary to the code of conduct issued by the commission for the by-election.

Mr Afridi had asked the high court to set aside the impugned notice. However, on Nov 26, the court dismissed both petitions, observing that no adverse order had so far been passed against the petitioners.

The bench had observed that it expected the ECP, in the first instance, to determine its jurisdiction in the matter before proceeding further with the inquiry.

Mr Afridi again approached the court earlier this year, contending that the ECP had been proceeding against him without first deciding the question of its jurisdiction, contrary to the Elections Act, 2017.

ECP counsel Khurram Shehzad argued that the petition was not maintainable and was liable to be dismissed as no order had so far been passed against the petitioner.

He submitted that the proceedings pending before the commission were independent in nature and separate from those pending before the district monitoring officer (DMO).

He argued that the ECP had two types of jurisdiction — one concerning civil wrongs and the other concerning cases of a criminal nature.

Under Section 15 of the Elections Act, 2017, he said, the ECP could take cognisance of matters relating to implementation of the code of conduct on its own motion as well as on a complaint filed by an aggrieved person.

He contended that an almost identical petition had been dismissed by the court in November last year.

Mr Afridi's counsel, Adnan Ali, stated that the ECP had issued the controversial notice to the chief minister on Nov 20, 2025.

"The allegation pertained to remarks made against election staff and influencing the election," he said.

"The speech delivered by the chief minister was outside the jurisdiction of NA-18 Haripur, where the by-election was held on Nov 23, 2025," the counsel argued.

He said that once the DMO had issued a notice to Mr Afridi under Section 234 of the Elections Act, the ECP lacked jurisdiction to issue another notice to him under Section 15 of the Act.

He argued that the ECP had clubbed a private complaint filed by a rival candidate with its suo motu proceedings. He contended that the ECP was exercising the powers of the DMO. "Here, both the ECP and the DMO issued notices, and the DMO also submitted a report to the former," he argued.

"Let the Election Commission hear you; present whatever your response is before them," Justice Arshad Ali remarked.

The bench observed, "This is merely an inquiry by the Election Commission, not a formal action. There is no legal bar preventing the Election Commission from conducting an inquiry."

However, Mr Afridi's lawyers maintained that the ECP had initiated a process under which the petitioner could face disqualification.
output: Peshawar High Court ne Wednesday ko Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ke Chief Minister Sohail Afridi ki request reject kar di. Yeh request Election Commission of Pakistan ke against action rokne ke liye thi. Election Commission of Pakistan woh idara hai jo mulk mein elections karwata hai. Yeh action November 2025 mein Haripur ke by-election mein election code of conduct todne ke ilzam par shuru kiya gaya tha. Election code of conduct woh rules hain jo elections ke dauran candidates aur government officials ko follow karne hote hain. Justice Syed Arshad Ali aur Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali ki bench ne chhota order jari kiya. Bench ne Election Commission ke jurisdiction ke sawal ko chhede baghair request dismiss kar di. Jurisdiction ka matlab hai ke kisi idare ya court ko kis mamle mein faisla karne ka ikhtiyar hai. Request reject hone ke saath Sohail Afridi ke haq mein pehle diya gaya stay order bhi khatam ho gaya. Stay order kisi faisle ya action par temporary rok hota hai. Misaal ke taur par, agar court kisi ke against action par rok laga de to usay stay order kehte hain. Sohail Afridi ne 20 November 2025 ko jari hone wale Election Commission ke notice ko challenge kiya tha. Is notice mein un par NA-18 Haripur ke by-election ke silsile mein government officials ke against bhadkane wali speech ka ilzam tha. Pichhle saal November mein Sohail Afridi aur PTI-backed candidate Shehrnaz Omar Ayub ne Election Commission ke notices challenge kiye the. 26 November ko court ne dono requests reject kar di. Sohail Afridi ke wakeelon mein Adnan Ali, Bashir Khan Wazir, Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah aur Inam Yousafzai shamil the. Election Commission ki taraf se Khurram Shehzad aur Samran Jehangir pesh hue. Shikayat karne wale ki taraf se Barrister Sajeel Sheharyar Swati pesh hue.

ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday summoned the Islamabad police chief and issued show-cause notices to two police officials over the continued failure to produce the case record in the security breach case against lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha.

Thecasepertains to the alleged disruption of a security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. Imaan and her husband were accused of removing barriers from the route. The couple wasindictedin the case on Oct 7.

During Saturday's hearing, ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain directed the two police officials to whom notices were issued to explain their failure to ensure the production of the record. He warned that they could face imprisonment if it was not presented before the court.

During the proceedings, the court expressed displeasure over the continued absence of the investigating officer and raised questions about the whereabouts of the case record.

A court official informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Gilgit-Baltistan and had not returned.

The judge immediately summoned the superintendent (investigation) to explain the situation.

Advocate Riasat Ali Azad, representing the accused, told the court that the bail application had been filed on October 29 last year and notices had already been issued, but the proceedings could not move forward because the investigating officer failed to appear with the record.

He argued that in similar cases, another police official usually appeared with the case record when the investigating officer was unavailable. Questioning how long the court was expected to wait, Azad urged the judge to make a decision in accordance with the law.

Advocate Asif Irfan, vice chairman of the Islamabad Bar Council, observed that the court was not powerless, but had so far been unable to ensure the production of the record.

Advocate Aleem Abbasi, meanwhile, urged the judge to exercise his authority and decide the matter on merit. He added that the legal fraternity stood with the judiciary in defending its independence, but questioned how lawyers could secure justice for their own children if the judicial system failed to deliver it.

Advocate Zafar Khokhar also questioned under which law an investigating officer could take the case record away and leave court proceedings stalled.

Judge Zulqarnain, however, expressed displeasure over the tone adopted by some lawyers, deeming such conduct inappropriate and remarking that he was not influenced by vlogs or commentary and always conducted proceedings impartially.

After a short break in the proceedings, SP Khurram Ashraf and Deputy Superintendent (DSP) Naeem Yousuf appeared before the court.

The SP informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Khaplu and would appear after he returned. The judge questioned the arrangement and asked when the officer would return, observing that everyone was waiting while the court had a case to decide.

When pressed for a definite timeline, DSP Yousuf said the investigating officer could take another 10 to 15 days to return.

The judge criticised the police for causing prolonged hardship to PTI workers through delays in their cases.

Expressing frustration over the situation and the alleged harassment of workers, the judge ordered the discharge of several individuals arrested in connection with the PTI's long march.

The court subsequently issued show-cause notices to the SP and DSP, warning that failure to produce the case record could lead to proceedings for their imprisonment.

Islamabad Inspector General of Police Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry was also summoned for the next hearing on November 3.

The lawyer couple has been in jail since theirarreston Jan 23 in acaseregistered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrestprompted criticismby rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple's right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions courtsentencedthem to 17 years on multiple charges under thePrevention of Electronic Crimes Act(Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts. The convictions werewidelycondemned bylawyersandUnited Nations (UN) experts.

On Sept 17, followingmonths of litigationbefore thecourts, the Supreme Courtsuspendedtheir sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC's final verdict on their appeals against the trial court's decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital's Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.
output: The Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) in Islamabad summoned Islamabad's police chief on Saturday. An anti-terrorism court is a court that hears cases linked to terrorism. The court issued show-cause notices to two police officers. A show-cause notice is a notice that asks someone to explain why action should not be taken against them. This case is against lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha. The charge is that they allegedly disrupted the security route of an international cricket team and caused public unrest. The couple was indicted in this case on October 7. Indicted means the court formally reads out the charges. After a break, SP Khurram Ashraf and DSP Naeem Yousuf appeared in court. The DSP said the investigating officer might take another 10 to 15 days to return. Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain ordered the release of several people arrested in PTI's long march. He also criticized the police for the delay. The court issued show-cause notices to the SP and DSP. The next hearing is on November 3, and the court has summoned Inspector General of Police Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry. The lawyer couple has been in jail since January 23 in a case with charges of protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the president of the IHC Bar Association. A sessions court had sentenced them to 17 years under Peca. On September 17, the Supreme Court suspended the sentence. A few hours later, police arrested them again in another case. This case was registered at Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

input:
Ahmed al Madhoun looked like a man who, despite the hardship, loved life. A cheeky, chunky little fellow with an exuberant smile.

From her partially destroyed home in Gaza City, his mother Majdiya shows us videos of him on her phone.

In one, Ahmed is cuddling a kitten. He sticks out his tongue and squeals with glee. In another, he belly flops into a swimming pool, before emerging from the water grinning from ear to ear.

"Everyone was his friend," Majdiya tells the BBC. "He was loved wherever he went, and he always had a smile on his face."

But Ahmed, who has Down's syndrome, is missing. The 21-year-old disappeared in May 2025 after popping to the local shop.

At the time, the war in Gaza between Hamas and Israel was raging.

That day there were Israeli strikes in the area, and Majdiya fears her son is dead. But she doesn't know for certain.

"My God, I am not at peace," she says. "I have not lost hope but whether they find him alive or dead, buried under the rubble, only then will I be at peace."

Pain like Majdiya's is felt by mothers all over Gaza.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign, including about 1,200 since a ceasefire was announced last October, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry - figures considered reliable by the UN.

Israeli media reported in January that a senior Israeli security source saidthe military accepts the figures are accurate.

But the true number of dead Palestinians could be significantly higher. The health ministry's death toll doesn't count bodies buried under the rubble, meaning many of the missing are not part of the count.

The Red Cross says it has received more than 5,000 requests to trace missing people who could be buried amid the destruction. The Civil Defence agency in Gaza believes the number of missing people is over 8,000.

Bodies are being discovered on a daily basis.

Earlier this month, a mass funeral took place in Gaza City for more than a hundred people killed in an Israeli attack in 2023. Their remains were only recently recovered and identified, allowing them to be laid to rest.

The Red Cross says recovering bodies is difficult given the scale of the destruction and a lack of bulldozers.

In many cases, identifying the remains is also challenging when people have been dead for so long and with a lack of DNA testing, due to Israeli restrictions on what can enter Gaza.

Ahmed al Madhoun's family knows he may well have been killed - but they also fear he may have been detained by Israeli security forces.

Over almost three years of war, Israeli forces have detained approximately 7,000 Palestinians from Gaza, more than 5,000 of whom were later released without ever being charged,according to the Israel-based Public Committee Against Torture,external.

As of this month, around 1,300 detainees from Gaza were being held in Israeli jails without charge or trial, according to the Israeli human rights group HaMoked. The group says these figures do not include Gaza detainees held directly by the Israeli military.

Palestinian families have frequently not been notified by Israel of the arrest or whereabouts of their relatives, according to HaMoked and other rights groups - forcing many to rely on NGOs and lawyers to help track them down.

The BBC has asked the IDF and Israel Prison Service (IPS) about their reported failure to contact relatives of those they have detained.

Israeli authorities have previously said prolonged detentions were due to wartime security grounds and rejected claims that detentions are arbitrary.

Aida al Drimli from the Sabra district of Gaza City, shows us a picture of her son, Mahmoud, a fresh-faced young man draped in a Palestinian scarf.

"He was a calm well-mannered young man," Aida says. "He loved everyone and everyone loved him."

Mahmoud disappeared in 2024. His family feared he had been killed in an Israeli attack.

"His father would go to the hospitals and look at the bodies," Aida tells us. "But I couldn't face it. I was completely devastated."

But then this summer a photo emerged on social media showing two Israeli soldiers posing with a Palestinian detainee, blindfolded and bound.
output: Ahmed al Madhoun was a 21-year-old young man. He had Down's syndrome. He went missing in Gaza City in May 2025. His mother Majdiya told the BBC that people liked Ahmed everywhere he went. He always smiled. According to the health ministry of Hamas, the Palestinian group that governs Gaza, more than 73,000 people were killed in Gaza after Israel's military campaign. This includes about 1,200 people killed after a ceasefire was announced last October. A ceasefire, or truce, means stopping the fighting. The Red Cross, an international aid organization, has received more than 5,000 requests to find missing people. Gaza's Civil Defence, which is the local emergency aid team, says the number of missing people is more than 8,000. The Red Cross said it is hard to pull bodies out of the rubble. It also said there is a lack of DNA testing because of Israeli restrictions. Israeli forces detained about 7,000 Palestinians from Gaza. More than 5,000 of them were released without charge. "Without charge or trial" means no one told them what crime they were arrested for, and no case was heard in court. According to HaMoked, a human rights group, this month about 1,300 prisoners from Gaza were being held in Israeli jails without charge or trial. Aida al Drimli said her son Mahmoud went missing in 2024. This summer, a photo appeared on social media of two Israeli soldiers with a Palestinian prisoner.

output: پاکستان کی عدالتِ عظمٰی نے وجیہہ الحسن کو بری کرنے کا حکم دیا ہے۔ عدالتِ عظمٰی پاکستان کی سب سے بڑی عدالت ہے۔ بری کرنے کا مطلب ہے الزام سے پاک قرار دینا۔ وجیہہ الحسن توہینِ مذہب کے مقدمے میں موت کی سزا پانے والے شخص تھے۔ توہینِ مذہب کا مطلب ہے مذہب کی بے حرمتی کا الزام۔ وہ 17 برس سے جیل میں تھے۔ عدالتِ عظمٰی نے انھیں عدم ثبوت کی بنیاد پر رہا کرنے کا حکم دیا۔ عدم ثبوت یعنی ایسے ٹھوس شواہد نہ ہونا جن سے الزام ثابت ہو۔ عدالتِ عظمٰی نے مسیحی خاتون آسیہ بی بی کو بھی رواں برس رہا کرنے کا حکم دیا تھا۔ آسیہ بی بی کے مقدمے میں بھی ٹھوس شواہد کی عدم موجودگی کو وجہ بتایا گیا تھا۔ ایسے کئی مقدمات سالہا سال سے ماتحت عدالتوں میں زیرِ التوا ہیں۔ ماتحت عدالتیں وہ چھوٹی عدالتیں ہیں جو بڑی عدالتوں سے نیچے ہوتی ہیں۔ بہاؤالدین زکریا یونیورسٹی ملتان کے استاد جنید حفیظ گذشتہ تقریباً 6 برس سے جیل میں ہیں اور فیصلے کے منتظر ہیں۔ جنید حفیظ کا مقدمہ لڑنے والے ایک وکیل قتل ہو چکے ہیں۔

instruction: Explain this news in Urdish (Urdu in Roman letters, mixed with common English words) for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
ISLAMABAD: The Int­e­r­national Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected Paki­stan's economic growth at 3.5 per cent during the current fiscal year, with inflation expected to remain close to double digits, even as global growth is forecast to rebound to 3.4pc in 2027.

In its flagship World Economic Outlook, released at the start of the World Bank-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, the Fund estimated Pakistan's current account deficit to widen to 1pc of GDP from a surplus of 0.5pc in FY25. Headline inflation is projected to rise to 9.9pc from 7.1pc last year.

However, the Washi­ngton-based lending age­ncy projected Pakistan's unemployment rate to dec­l­ine to 6.5pc this year compared to 6.9pc last year and 7.1pc a year earlier. The IMF, which concluded its review of Pakistan's economic situation last week, did not explain the projected decline in unemployment despite the rising population and its other economic forecasts, including higher inflation and a widening current account deficit.

The Fund's growth projections are significantly lower than the government's 4pc target for the current year and the 3.8pc forecast by the World Bank last month. Its estimated 3.5pc growth rate for Pakistan is slightly lower than the 3.6pc recorded last year but higher than the 3.2pc in FY25.

Saying global economic activity had proved resilient despite multiple challenges, the international lender projected global growth to slow to 3.1pc in 2026 before rebounding to 3.4pc in 2027. Global headline inflation is projected to rise notably to 4.7pc in 2026 before easing to 4.1pc in 2027, it added.

The IMF attributed global economic resilience to the technology upturn, buffers and adaptations that helped mitigate the damage from geopolitics-driven disruptions.

"In less than seven years, the global economy has been subjected to an exceptional sequence of events. The pandemic and the ensuing disruptions to global supply chains; the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, with the consequent sharp increases in the prices of energy and other commodities; and significant changes in trade barriers and trading relations have tested the resilience of households, firms, financial markets and governments," it said.

"Individually, each of these major developments would have been considered unlikely. Their confluence over such a short period of time is even more extraordinary. Yet, desp­ite this barrage of shocks, the global economy has held up," the IMF said.

It added that labour markets had remained unexpectedly strong, financial systems had broadly withstood the shocks and the sharpest monetary tightening in half a century, while inflation had receded from its peaks in many economies, although it remained persistent in some cases.

The IMF warned that energy-importing economies like Pakistan, which have limited links to the technology value chain, face the most difficult outlook. However, the margins of adjustment that have helped sustain resilience are not limitless and risks are skewed to the downside, it said.

Further escalation in conflicts, a reassessment of expectations surrounding artificial intelligence, renewed trade tensions and fiscal vulnerabilities could weaken growth. On the upside, stronger AI investment and productivity gains, or a sustained easing of geopolitical and trade tensions, could support growth.

The Fund advised its members that fiscal frameworks must deliver better results in dealing with disruptive shocks and build policy space through revenue measures. During cost-of-living crises, governments should preserve price signals and rely primarily on temporary, targeted income support for the most vulnerable, it said.

The stable global aggregate masks a reallocation of growth across economies. Countries with limited direct exposure to the war shock and strong participation in the technology uptu­­rn are seeing activity hold up or stre­n­­gthen. Energy exporters outside the immediate conflict zone are benefiting from favourable terms of trade.

Conversely, energy-importing economies with little connection to the technology value chain face the most difficult combination of higher import costs and exchange rate pressures, weaker real incomes, more constrained fiscal space and fewer offsetting demand impulses.

Many low-income and vulnerable countries belong to this latter group, increasing the risk that recent shocks will widen income gaps across and within countries.

The IMF projected world trade volume growth to slow in 2026 and stabilise in 2027, reflecting the drag from tariffs, adjustments in production chains and continued strength in technology-related trade.

A day earlier, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told Reuters that the government expected the economy to grow by more than 4pc this fiscal year despite elevated oil prices. He also said the government was looking to privatise five to six entities during the year, potentially raising more than $1 billion.
output: IMF ne kaha hai ke is financial year mein Pakistan ki economy 3.5 per cent barhegi. IMF ek international financial institution hai jo mulkon ko loan aur advice deta hai. IMF ke mutabiq Pakistan mein inflation 7.1 per cent se barh kar 9.9 per cent ho jayegi. Inflation ka matlab hai ke prices lagatar barhti rehti hain. Misaal ke taur par, agar aate ki price har mahine barhti rahe to yeh inflation hai. IMF ne andaza lagaya hai ke Pakistan ka current account deficit FY25 mein 0.5 per cent surplus se barh kar GDP ke 1 per cent ho jayega. Current account deficit ka matlab hai ke mulk bahar se jo paisa lata hai us se zyada bahar bhej raha ho. GDP ka matlab hai kisi mulk mein ek saal mein tayyar hone wali tamam cheezon aur services ki total value. IMF ne kaha hai ke Pakistan mein is saal unemployment rate kam ho kar 6.5 per cent ho jayega, jo pichhle saal 6.9 per cent tha. IMF ki growth forecast government ke 4 per cent target aur World Bank ki 3.8 per cent forecast se kam hai. World Bank ek international institution hai jo development projects mein madad deta hai. IMF ne kaha hai ke global growth 2026 mein 3.1 per cent rahegi aur 2027 mein 3.4 per cent tak barhegi. IMF ne warning di hai ke Pakistan jaisi energy import karne wali economies ka outlook sab se mushkil hai. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb ne Reuters ko bataya ke government ko is financial year mein 4 per cent se zyada growth ki umeed hai aur woh 5 se 6 entities private sector ko bechna chahti hai.

instruction: Explain this news in Urdu (Urdu script) for a reader with no knowledge of international relations: explain the key terms and actors in simple words.
input:
For technology companies, the super app is the holy grail: one application that becomes the starting point for a consumer's digital life. Messaging brings people in every day. Payments, shopping, transport, financial services, and finally government services keep them there. Few companies in the world have managed to make this work at scale.

WeChat is the obvious example. It began with messaging and expanded into an ecosystem of payments, commerce and services. However, WeChat succeeded because the Chinese government banned WhatsApp and other messaging services.

Should Pakistan simply order a WeChat of its own? Our digital lives remain fragmented between messaging applications. WhatsApp is the top-ranked messaging platform by far. Among bank accounts and wallets, Easypaisa and JazzCash both claim 100 million cumulative downloads; among shopping platforms, Daraz is the local e-commerce leader. The government-related services portal, Pak ID, leads the way among government apps.

Pakistan has tried the super app route before. In 2017, Veon launched its application with Jazz, combining communications, content, offers and eventually financial services. Profit reported at the time that spending on the initiative had exceeded $100 million. Despite Jazz's customer base and Veon's financial resources, the application failed to become Pakistan's WeChat and was eventually withdrawn.

The lesson is important. Money and distribution alone do not create a super app. A telecom company can offer free data and spend heavily on acquisition, but it cannot easily persuade families, friends and businesses to abandon a messaging platform they already use every day. A super app first needs a compelling reason for daily engagement. Everything else follows. There is also a broader national issue.

Much of Pakistan's digital communication, commerce and even official business passes through foreign platforms. Governments face risks when sensitive official communication and public records sit beyond their effective control. Where is the information stored? Who can access it? How is it preserved? What happens if a foreign platform changes its policies or becomes unavailable?

Some governments have responded by restricting the use of consumer messaging applications for official communication. France has directed ministers and staff towards approved secure systems rather than applications such as WhatsApp. Britain has issued guidance around the use of non-corporate communication channels for government business.

Pakistan should distinguish between consumer choice and official communication. There may be little logic in trying to force citizens away from WhatsApp. However, government communications, sensitive records and critical public data deserve stronger safeguards.

Pakistan already possesses many of the building blocks required for a broader digital ecosystem.

Nadra provides identity infrastructure, biometric verification and digital identity services. Its Nishan Pakistan platform allows regulated organisations to use services including fingerprint and facial verification, demographic verification and proof of life. These capabilities can help citizens establish identity without requiring Nadra itself to operate their banking, shopping or messaging applications.
output: ٹیکنالوجی کمپنیوں کے لیے سپر ایپ ایک مقدس مقصد ہے۔ سپر ایپ ایسی ایپ ہوتی ہے جس میں کئی کام ایک جگہ ہوں، جیسے میسجنگ، پیمنٹ، خریداری اور خدمات۔ وی چیٹ اس کی واضح مثال ہے۔ اس نے میسجنگ سے پیمنٹس، کامرس اور سروسز تک توسیع کی۔ وی چیٹ کامیاب ہوا کیونکہ چینی حکومت نے واٹس ایپ اور دیگر میسجنگ سروسز پر پابندی لگائی، یعنی ان کے استعمال پر روک۔ پاکستان میں ڈیجیٹل زندگی میسجنگ ایپس کے درمیان بکھری ہوئی ہے، اور واٹس ایپ سب سے آگے ہے۔ ایزی پیسہ اور جاز کیش دونوں 100 ملین مجموعی ڈاؤن لوڈز کا دعویٰ کرتے ہیں۔ ڈراز مقامی ای کامرس میں سب سے آگے ہے، اور پاک آئی ڈی حکومتی ایپس میں آگے ہے۔ 2017 میں ویون نے جاز کے ساتھ ایک ایپ لانچ کی۔ پرافٹ کے مطابق اس پر 100 ملین ڈالر سے زیادہ خرچ ہوا۔ جاز کے صارفین اور ویون کے مالی وسائل کے باوجود یہ ایپ پاکستان کا وی چیٹ نہ بن سکی اور بعد میں واپس لے لی گئی۔ کیونکہ صرف پیسہ اور تقسیم سپر ایپ نہیں بناتے۔ پاکستان کو صارفین کی پسند اور سرکاری مواصلات میں فرق کرنا چاہیے۔ فرانس نے وزرا اور عملے کو واٹس ایپ جیسی ایپس کے بجائے منظور شدہ محفوظ نظاموں کی طرف ہدایت دی۔ برطانیہ نے حکومتی کاروبار کے لیے غیر کارپوریٹ مواصلاتی چینلز پر رہنمائی جاری کی، یعنی ایسے ذریعے جو کسی کمپنی کے بنائے ہوئے عام ایپس نہ ہوں۔ نادرا شناختی ڈھانچہ، بائیو میٹرک تصدیق اور ڈیجیٹل شناخت کی خدمات دیتا ہے۔ نشان پاکستان پلیٹ فارم قواعد ماننے والی تنظیموں کو فنگر پرنٹ اور چہرے کی تصدیق، آبادیاتی تصدیق اور پروف آف لائف جیسی سہولیات استعمال کرنے دیتا ہے۔

input:
پاکستان میں ٹیکس پالیسیاں نافذ کرنے اور ٹیکس وصولی کے ذمہ دار ادارے فیڈرل بورڈ آف ریوینیو (ایف بی آر) نے غیر ملکیوں سمیت سوشل میڈیا انفلوئنسرز کی آمدنی اور اس پر ٹیکس کا حساب لگانے کے متعلق نئے قواعد جاری کر دیے ہیں۔

ایف بی آر کی جانب سے 23 ستمبر کو جاری کردہ نوٹیفکیشنز کے مطابق انکم ٹیکس آرڈیننس کے سیکشن 99 'سپیشل پراسیجر' کے تحت سوشل میڈیا کے ذریعے آمدن کمانے والے افراد کو ٹیکس نیٹ میں شامل کیا گیا ہے۔

نئے قواعد کے تحت کسی بھی مالی سال کے لیے سوشل میڈیا مواد سے آمدن کا تعین کرنے کے لیے مجموعی معاوضے میں سے آمدن کے زیادہ سے زیادہ 30 فیصد اخراجات منہا کرنے کی اجازت دی گئی ہے۔

ایف بی آر کا کہنا ہے کہ مجموعی آمدن کا حساب لگانے کے لیے دو طریقے وضع کیے گئے ہیں۔

صحافی تنویر ملک سے بات کرتے ہوئے ایف بی آر کے ترجمان نے بتایا کہ نئے قواعد کے تحت 'آمدن کا تعین دو اعداد میں سے زیادہ رقم کی بنیاد پر کیا جائے گا: یا تو ویوز کی تعداد کو حکومت کی جانب سے مقرر کردہ 195 روپے فی ہزار ویوز یا ریوینیو پر مائل (آر پی ایم) کی شرح سے ضرب دے کر حاصل ہونے والی رقم، یا حقیقت میں نقد یا اشیا و خدمات کی صورت میں حاصل ہونے والی رقم۔'

انھوں نے بتایا کہ ویوز کی تعداد عوامی طور پر دستیاب ہوتی ہے اور اس کی آزادانہ طور پر تصدیق کی جا سکتی ہے۔ 'اس لیے تخلیق کار کی جانب سے ظاہر کی جانے والی آمدن اس مقررہ حد سے کم نہیں ہو سکتی، تاوقتیکہ وہ کم آمدن کا ثبوت کمشنر کے سامنے پیش نہ کرے۔'

تاہم خیال رہے کہ بیشتر کانٹینٹ کریئیٹرز کی جانب سے روزانہ کی بنیاد پر ویڈیوز جاری کی جاتی ہیں ایک، ایک کر کے جن کے ویوز کی گنتی کرنا کافی مشکل کام ہے۔

ایف بی آر کے مطابق اس شرح میں وقتاً فوقتاً تبدیلی کی جا سکتی ہے۔

ترجمان کا کہنا تھا کہ سپانسرز کی جانب سے اشیا، سفری سہولیات یا خدمات کی صورت میں ملنے والی ادائیگیوں کو بھی ان کی منصفانہ مارکیٹ ویلیو کے مطابق آمدن تصور کیا جائے گا۔ یہ انکم ٹیکس آرڈیننس کی دفعہ 18 (1)(d) کے تحت آمدن میں شامل ہے۔

نوٹیفکیشن میں کہا گیا ہے کہ اگر کوئی انفلوئنسر مؤقف اختیار کرتا ہے کہ اسے حقیقت میں موصول ہونے والا معاوضہ آر پی ایم کے تحت متعین رقم سے کم ہے تو اسے اپنے دعوے کے حق میں ثبوت ٹیکس کمشنر کو فراہم کرنے ہوں گے۔

نئے قواعد کے تحت اس طریقۂ کار کے دائرہ کار میں آنے والے ہر شخص کے لیے سہ ماہی بنیادوں پر پیشگی انکم ٹیکس کی ادائیگی بھی لازم ہو گی۔

ایف بی آر کا کہنا ہے کہ اگر ظاہر کی گئی آمدن خصوصی طریقۂ کار کے تحت متعین ہونے والی رقم سے کم ہو تو متعلقہ کمشنر ٹیکس گوشوارے میں موجود کمی یا غلطی کی درستی کر سکتا ہے اور واجب الادا رقم وصول کر سکتا ہے۔
output: فیڈرل بورڈ آف ریوینیو (ایف بی آر)، جو ٹیکس جمع کرنے والا ادارہ ہے، نے غیر ملکیوں سمیت سوشل میڈیا انفلوئنسرز کی آمدنی اور ٹیکس کے حساب کے لیے نئے قواعد جاری کیے ہیں۔ ایف بی آر نے 23 ستمبر کو نوٹیفکیشنز، یعنی سرکاری نوٹس، جاری کیے۔ نئے قواعد انکم ٹیکس آرڈیننس کے سیکشن 99 'سپیشل پراسیجر' کے تحت جاری کیے گئے ہیں۔ انکم ٹیکس آرڈیننس وہ قانون ہے جس کے تحت آمدنی پر ٹیکس لگتا ہے۔ سیکشن 99 'سپیشل پراسیجر' اس قانون کا وہ حصہ ہے جو کچھ خاص معاملات کے لیے الگ طریقہ بتاتا ہے۔ نئے قواعد کے تحت سوشل میڈیا مواد سے آمدن کے تعین کے لیے مجموعی معاوضے میں سے زیادہ سے زیادہ 30 فیصد اخراجات منہا کرنے کی اجازت ہے۔ ایف بی آر کے ترجمان نے صحافی تنویر ملک کو بتایا کہ آمدن کا تعین دو اعداد میں سے زیادہ رقم کی بنیاد پر کیا جائے گا۔ ایک رقم ویوز کی تعداد کو حکومت کی جانب سے مقرر کردہ 195 روپے فی ہزار ویوز یا ریوینیو پر مائل (آر پی ایم) کی شرح سے ضرب دے کر حاصل ہوگی، یا حقیقت میں نقد یا اشیا و خدمات کی صورت میں حاصل ہونے والی رقم ہوگی۔ ریوینیو پر مائل (آر پی ایم) کا مطلب ہے فی ہزار ویوز پر ملنے والی رقم۔ ترجمان کے مطابق اسپانسرز کی اشیا، سفری سہولیات یا خدمات کی صورت میں ادائیگیاں منصفانہ مارکیٹ ویلیو کے مطابق آمدن تصور ہوں گی اور یہ انکم ٹیکس آرڈیننس کی دفعہ 18 (1)(d) کے تحت آمدن میں شامل ہیں۔ نئے قواعد کے تحت دائرہ کار میں آنے والے ہر شخص کو سہ ماہی بنیادوں پر پیشگی انکم ٹیکس ادا کرنا لازم ہوگا۔ پیشگی انکم ٹیکس کا مطلب ہے ٹیکس سال کے دوران ہی قسطوں میں ٹیکس جمع کرانا۔

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo XIV spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin by phone on Friday, calling for a ceasefire in a Russian-occupied city in southern Ukraine, as he recovers in hospital from alung canceroperation.

The Vatican said that Pope Leo "expressed his deep concern about the grave humanitarian situation in the city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, and called for a ceasefire to allow the delivery of food and medical assistance, and the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population".

The surprise notice from the Vatican on Friday evening suggested that the recovering pope is still hard at work, despite this week's operation to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung.

Residents of Oleshky, in southern Ukraine, are facing a worsening humanitarian crisis with shortages of food and medication as they are caught in the crossfire between Russian and Ukrainian troops.

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Turk, denounced a "desperate" situation in the city, calling on Russia to enable civilians to evacuate.

In a note, the Kremlin said the two had talked and "a detailed explanation was provided regarding the Kyiv regime's responsibility for the difficult humanitarian situation" in Oleshky.

The Kremlin said Putin also wished the pope a speedy recovery and stressed the "importance of Russian-Vatican cooperation in promoting unifying spiritual and moral values".

Earlier in the day, the pontiff celebrated mass on the top floor of Rome's Gemelli hospital, as seen in the first images of him released by the Vatican since the procedure.

The images showed the 71-year-old Chicago-born pope in front of a makeshift altar in a room on the 10th floor, dressed in a green vestment.

He appeared relaxed and in good form in the two photos released, standing with his private secretary, Peruvian priest Edgard Rimaycuna, at his side.

ISLAMABAD: The So­­ciety of the Inner Temple in the United Kingdom has welcomed Chief Justi­ce of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi as an Honorary Bencher at its Benchers' Night in London.

The occasion provided an opportunity to explore ways to strengthen institutional cooperation between the judicial and legal institutions of Pakistan and the United Kingdom through the exchange of knowledge, experience and professional expertise, according to a press release.

Discussions focused on judicial capacity-building, particularly in case management and judgement writing, as well as opportunities to enhance professional standards in legal ethics and advocacy. These areas offer scope for closer engagement and mutual learning between the two jurisdictions.

Continued institutional cooperation can facilitate the exchange of best practices, strengthen judicial skills and promote professionalism within the legal community.

The Chief Justice's association with the Inner Temple as an Honorary Bencher provides a valuable link for fostering these exchanges and further strengthening ties betwe­­en the legal communities of Pakistan and the United Kingdom.
